title: Share the judge findings cap between judge-run and the verdict panel
body:
## Summary
The Judge verdict panel re-types the 1500-character storage cap that the judge runner applies as a bare literal.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/steps/ux/judgeVerdictRecord.ts:18 declares STORED_FINDINGS_CAP = 1500 and uses it at :49 to decide a record was clipped; scripts/judge-run.ts:411 writes .slice(0, 1500) as a literal. If the runner's cap moves, the panel misreports clipping and quotes the wrong number. Fixed: one exported constant both read. The fix edits a script outside this context.

## Flow
- Export the cap from a module both sides can import
- scripts/judge-run.ts and judgeVerdictRecord.ts read it
- Test: moving the constant moves the clipped decision

## Expected impact
An operator reading a clipped verdict keeps a truthful "cut off at N" line. Nothing else changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one storage cap instead of two
Before: 2 literal sites of 1500
After: 1 constant (predicted)
Method: simulation - read both sites; the writer is out of this round's paths so the change was not applied
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: An operator reading a clipped verdict keeps a truthful "cut off at N" line. Nothing else changes.
instrument: vi.mock the shared constant to a new value and assert parseFindings.clipped follows it; grep scripts/judge-run.ts for no literal 1500

title: Export the sibling omission heading instead of re-typing it in the desk
body:
## Summary
The sibling-check desk parses a heading string that it re-types from siblingSteps.ts, so a wording change misreports what the prompt dropped.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/steps/ux/siblingReconcile.ts:29 hard-codes 'Omitted by prompt size cap'; src/lib/catalog/siblingSteps.ts:34 writes it inside omissionBlock and does not export it. If the heading changes, promptReach finds no dropped labels and reachOf returns 'absent', so a produced sibling reads "— no output" and the unseen warning vanishes. The module header says the reach "cannot drift", which holds for the block but not for this heading. siblingSteps.ts belongs to catalog-core-infrastructure.

## Flow
- Export the heading constant from siblingSteps.ts
- siblingReconcile.ts imports it
- Existing siblingReconcile.test.ts stays green

## Expected impact
The dropped-sibling warning survives a prompt wording change. One added export; no behaviour change today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - parser reads the writer's heading
Before: 2 copies of the heading, 1 unexported
After: 1 exported constant (predicted)
Method: simulation - read both sites; the writer is out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The dropped-sibling warning survives a prompt wording change. One added export; no behaviour change today.
instrument: vi.mock the heading constant to new text and assert real siblingStepsBlock output still parses as dropped

title: One-shot drawer declares aria-modal with no Escape, focus trap or restore
body:
## Summary
OneShotPanel hand-rolls a modal drawer and its scrim, claiming aria-modal without the behaviour the shared Modal supplies.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/one-shot/OneShotPanel.tsx:96-102 paints a fixed full-screen rgba scrim and role="dialog" aria-modal="true". The file has no Escape or keydown handler (grep: 0) and no focus trap or restore, so keyboard focus moves behind a surface announced as modal. The guard no-hand-rolled-dialog-scrim.test.ts matches the class 'fixed inset-0' only, so this inline position/inset spelling is invisible to it, and role="dialog" would satisfy it anyway. Fixed: the drawer gains Modal's guarantees, through Modal if it can host a right-rail layout, else a shared drawer shell.

## Flow
- Open the one-shot panel
- Press Escape: nothing happens
- Press Tab repeatedly: focus leaves the dialog
- Fix: reuse Modal behaviour; widen the guard to the inline spelling

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users can leave and stay inside the drawer. Risk: existing OneShotPanel tests and the click-away scrim.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the drawer behaves as the dialog it announces
Before: 0 Escape handlers, 0 focus-trap code in OneShotPanel.tsx
After: not measured
Method: simulation - read and grepped; a port needs a decision on the drawer shell, so no probe was applied
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users can leave and stay inside the drawer. Risk: existing OneShotPanel tests and the click-away scrim.
instrument: Component test: Escape closes, Tab wraps within the dialog, focus returns to the opener on close

title: One-shot panels sit under the lab type floor at 54 inline sizes
body:
## Summary
The one-shot folder sets 54 inline font sizes of 10-13px where the lab documents a 14px floor.

## Description
The manifest and StepFrame state type >= 14px for lab controls and step UI. src/components/layout-lab/one-shot/ has 54 inline fontSize values of 10-13 (ProposalView 8, ProposalLanding 8, CatalogPickerForm 7, RunPlanView 7, RunLogView 6, AnalyzedView 5, DistributionView 4, OneShotPanel 4, ProposalIssues 4, RunActions 1); ESLint warns on the three in RunLogView below its 12px floor. Whether a 380px drawer is meant to follow the 14px floor is unconfirmed.

## Flow
- Decide the drawer's floor
- Move sizes to the lab scale per occurrence

## Expected impact
Run reasons and plan rows get easier to read; the 380px drawer gets denser, which could wrap rows.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - legible one-shot text
Before: 54 sites below 14px, 3 below 12px
After: not measured
Method: simulation - counted by grep; a bulk resize needs a visual check this round may not run
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Run reasons and plan rows get easier to read; the 380px drawer gets denser, which could wrap rows.
instrument: Source-scan ratchet on inline font sizes under one-shot/, plus a screenshot of the drawer at 380px

title: Give bespoke Items step frames the version history generic steps have
body:
## Summary
StaticStepFrame and GenerativeStepFrame omit StepHistoryPanel, so a bespoke Items step has no compare or restore.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/steps/ArchetypeStep.tsx:544 renders StepHistoryPanel under Raw artifact. src/components/layout-lab/steps/StaticStepFrame.tsx:98 and GenerativeStepFrame.tsx Raw artifact panels do not (grep: 0 in both). The seven bespoke labels persist to the same pipeline_artifacts rows, so revisions may exist with no window on them. Whether the bespoke lab store path reaches upsertArtifact for every write was not traced.

## Flow
- Open an Items bespoke step such as Attributes
- Raw artifact shows no previous versions
- Fix: append StepHistoryPanel with catalogId items in both frames

## Expected impact
A re-produced bespoke step becomes recoverable from its own screen. Loaded on demand, so no added fetch on mount.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - restore reaches the bespoke steps
Before: 0 of 2 bespoke frames render history; 1 of 1 generic does
After: 2 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - grep of the three frames; revision rows for bespoke labels not sampled
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A re-produced bespoke step becomes recoverable from its own screen. Loaded on demand, so no added fetch on mount.
instrument: Render test that a bespoke step shows the history panel, plus a count of pipeline_artifact_revisions rows for bespoke labels

title: All-failed one-shot toast names a step the run did not stop at
body:
## Summary
When every step fails, the toast reads "failed at step N/N" although the run did not stop at step N.

## Description
src/lib/one-shot/orchestrator.ts emits oneshot.failed with stepIndex: steps.length - 1 and error 'all steps failed' after the whole loop ran; src/components/layout-lab/one-shot/toastHandler.ts renders it as "failed at step 12/12 — all steps failed". The index is a placeholder rendered as a location. Fixed: the event marks a whole-run failure and the toast words it without a step. The orchestrator belongs to another context.

## Flow
- Run a one-shot where every step fails
- Toast reads failed at step N/N
- Fix: optional stepIndex on the event; toast omits the position when absent

## Expected impact
The failure toast stops pointing at the last step as the culprit. An in-tree event payload change with 1 toast consumer found.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - toast states what the run recorded
Before: 1 reproduced-by-reading sentence naming a fabricated position
After: not measured
Method: simulation - read emitter and toast; the emitter is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The failure toast stops pointing at the last step as the culprit. An in-tree event payload change with 1 toast consumer found.
instrument: toastHandler test with a whole-run failure payload asserting no "step N/N" text

title: Histogram view draws an absent bucket as a zero bar; bars drop it
body:
## Summary
The generic chart view handles a missing key two ways: bars omit it, the histogram paints it as zero.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/steps/ArchetypeStep.tsx:162-165 drops a row whose value does not decode; :171 maps the same case to num(rec[k]) ?? 0, so a key the artifact never recorded renders as a measured zero. For a distribution, absent may legitimately mean zero, so the right rule is a product call per step. 3 grep hits for variant: 'histogram' under src/lib/catalog, at least one of them a type or doc line.

## Flow
- Store a histogram record missing one declared key
- A zero-height slot renders, identical to a recorded 0
- Fix: decide absent vs zero, then distinguish or drop

## Expected impact
A histogram stops implying a measurement for an unrecorded bucket. Dropping shifts bar positions, which carry no labels today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - absent is not zero
Before: bars omit, histogram coerces to 0
After: not measured
Method: simulation - read both branches; the intended meaning of absent needs a decision
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
impact: A histogram stops implying a measurement for an unrecorded bucket. Dropping shifts bar positions, which carry no labels today.
instrument: Sample stored histogram artifacts for missing declared keys; if none, reject

title: Move the 11 raw one-shot buttons onto LabButton or the focus-ring class
body:
## Summary
All 11 raw buttons in the one-shot folder lack the .focus-ring class that LabButton carries.

## Description
The manifest routes lab buttons through LabButton, which sets .focus-ring and type="button". src/components/layout-lab/one-shot/ has 11 raw <button> elements (AnalyzedView 2, CatalogPickerForm 2, ProposalView 2, DistributionView 1, OneShotPanel 1, ProposalIssues 1, ProposalLanding 1, RunPlanView 1); the only focus-ring uses in the folder are on the hint input, catalog select and refine textarea. Two buttons (CatalogPickerForm:114, ProposalView Refine/Run) also omit type="button", harmless outside a form. Whether a browser default outline already shows was not checked.

## Flow
- Tab through the one-shot drawer
- Compare the focus indicator with LabButton controls
- Fix: LabButton where the look fits, else add focus-ring

## Expected impact
Keyboard focus reads the same across the lab. Risk: small visual shifts in the drawer.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - consistent visible focus
Before: 0 of 11 raw buttons carry focus-ring
After: 11 of 11 (predicted)
Method: simulation - grep counts; focus rendering needs a browser
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Keyboard focus reads the same across the lab. Risk: small visual shifts in the drawer.
instrument: Source-scan test: every <button> under one-shot/ carries focus-ring or is a LabButton
